To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have crystallized and determined the crystallographic properties of the 13 subunit portal protein of SPP1.
the portal protein from bacteriophage Spp1 was crystallized and its structure determined at a resolution of 2.5 angstroms.

1) we have crystallized the 13-fold portal protein of bacterio-phage SPP1; 2) the crystals diffract to high resolution; 3) the asymmetric unit contains one 13-fold symmetric protein; 4) we have determined the unit cell dimensions and space group of the crystals; 5) we have determined that the protein crystallizes in the presence of polyethylene glycol (PEG) 400 and 1.5 M ammonium sulfate;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crystallization of a 13-fold symmetric protein and the preliminary analysis of the diffraction data.
the structural analysis of the portal protein of SPP1, which may provide insights into the mechanism of DNA packaging.
the structural and functional characterization of the portal protein of bacterio-phage SPP1.

the crystallization conditions were selected based upon the physico-chemical properties of the portal protein in different ionic environment.
the crystal structure of the 13 subunits of gp6 will be the first to be determined and will reveal the molecular architecture of the portal complex of a large bacteriophage.
the crystallization of the SPP1 gp6 protein was achieved and that the crystals diffract to a high resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to crystallize the SPP1 portal proteins and to collect diffraction data up 7.85A resolution.
the 13-fold portal protein of SPP1 was successfully crystallized.
we have obtained the first X-ray crystallography data from the portal proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the salt conditions used in crystallization of the gp6 are very important in determining the crystal form of the protein.
the ionic environment of the crystallized proteins is an important factor for the crystallization of proteins with multiple symmetry axes.
the salt condition of the protein solution is critical for the crystallization of the portal protein.
